question: A hallucination is a misinterpretation of an existing external stimulus, while an illusion is a sensory perception without any external stimulus.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: The definitions are reversed. A hallucination has no real external stimulus; an illusion is a distorted perception of a stimulus that actually exists. This distinction is critical when documenting symptoms in a forensic psychiatric assessment.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — that is the reversal. An illusion is the misinterpretation of a real external stimulus (e.g. seeing a face in curtain folds), whereas a hallucination arises with no external stimulus at all (e.g. hearing a voice in a silent room).
